note: THE PARAGRAPHPLAN JUDGE'S AXES (kogaki#1533, owner decision 2026-10-23): one responsibility and one sentence per axis, rendered in this order into `paragraph_plan_judge_unit` by its `{{axes}}` token (src/workflow/judge.mjs).

Each axis carries `fixtures`: at least one `defect` record that violates this axis and no other, and one `clean` record, each naming a record under `records`. A record is a judge input whole, one Leg under its one bound Move (kogaki#1777), or `from` another record with one `edit`: a Waypoint replaced (`paragraph`, `waypoint`, `to`), a `join` replaced (`paragraph`, `join`), or the bound Move's `takes` or `leaves` replaced (`move_takes` or `move_leaves`) (kogaki#1701). `at_paragraph` names the paragraph a defect sits on.

THE RETENTION RULE: an axis is kept where, over at least `retention.draws_min` draws of `node src/proof-sheet/judge-bench.mjs --axis <id>`, its defect records are refused in at least `defect_refused_with_min` of the draws with the axis and in at most `defect_refused_without_max` without it, and its clean record passes in at least `clean_passed_with_min` with it; an axis failing the rule is removed. Rates are fractions of the draws.

`justified_by` records the bench run that kept the axis: its date, its run directory and its rates. `judge-bench.mjs --record` writes it, or removes the axis that fails the rule; checks/check-paragraph-plan-axes.sh refuses an axis without it.
Countable rules are not axes: the Waypoint count against the bound Move's Segments and the one-of `performs` and `point` are refusals of the plan-record validator (src/paragraph-plan.mjs).

segments.manner: a single short declaration offered without support or qualification

segments.operation: names one concrete instance habitually used to make a general point visible

paragraph_waypoints.point: A set of automatic rules can be written with every care and still never act on an entire kind of action.

The instance that makes this plainest is a set of rules that runs on every write to a record and not once on that record's deletion, such a set being a standing arrangement in a system that acts by itself whenever an action of a kind it was set up for happens, and a write and a deletion each being an action, one thing done in a system of a kind that can be named.

That instance is put together out of nothing unusual, an ordinary set of rules and two ordinary actions, and what it makes plain is that the care taken in writing the rules decided nothing about the kind of action they passed over.
The same instance also accounts for a second matter, why deleting that record raises no warning at all, since nothing in the set was ever set up to notice a deletion.

paragraph_waypoints.point: Which single thing decides whether a standing set of automatic rules does anything at all about something that happens?
It is the kind the happening belongs to.
A home burglar alarm is wired against certain kinds of opening at an entry point of the house.

So every kind of opening at an entry point of the house falls on one side of that wiring or the other, and an upstairs window of an unwired kind can stand open the whole night with the alarm quiet, because that opening fits none of the patterns the alarm was given and is therefore no concern of its.
Of everything that could be said about such an arrangement, the line between the kinds it was signed up against and the kinds it was not is the most important thing about it.
